claims.text: MITRE's Board of Trustees elected former Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence Donald Kerr as chairman, reported 6 November 2018, at the same meeting that elected former Rep. Mike Rogers, ex-chairman of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, as vice chairman.

claims.source: Public ODNI and NRO biographical record, as summarised in WashingtonExec's 2018 report on his MITRE election
claims.text: Kerr previously directed Los Alamos National Laboratory and the National Reconnaissance Office before becoming PDDNI.

Kerr's career is recited on the record at his own confirmation hearing before the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence on 1 August 2007: 'Deputy Assistant Secretary for Defense Programs at the Department of Energy. Federal Bureau of Investigation's Assistant Director in Charge, Laboratory Division. Deputy Director for Science and Technology at the Central Intelligence Agency. Director of the National Reconnaissance Office, where he currently serves.'

The same hearing records that 'Don began his government career at the Los Alamos National Lab in 1966 and worked his way up through the Lab and the Department of Energy, eventually becoming Director of Los Alamos'. The national-laboratory to black-space progression the board describes is therefore the Senate's own account of him, not an inference.

A committee member characterised the agency Kerr then led as 'the National Reconnaissance Office, which unfortunately is one of the more troubled and poorly performing agencies within the intelligence community.'

label: Donald M. Kerr
narrative: Kerr's career is the FFRDC-to-black-space pipeline in a single resume, and it runs straight through two of the locations this board cares about most. He directed Los Alamos National Laboratory - the contractor-operated DOE laboratory where the February 1949 green fireballs conference was convened and whose National Security Research Center still holds those minutes. He then served as Director of the National Reconnaissance Office, the agency that owns the overhead collection architecture through which any persistent anomalous object would be detected and, if desired, buried. He then became Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence from 2007 to 2009. In November 2018 MITRE's Board of Trustees elected him its chairman. He was previously an FBI assistant director for the laboratory division and a senior executive at SAIC. Every rung of that ladder is an institution named in the legacy-programme allegations: LANL, NRO, ODNI, SAIC, MITRE. Kerr has never publicly said anything about UAP. The point is not that he has; the point is that when Congress finally addresses a records demand to MITRE, the board culture it is addressing was shaped by a man who ran the NRO.
